name: Close-Grip Neutral T-Bar Row
description: The close-grip neutral T-bar row uses a parallel/neutral grip with hands close together, allowing the elbows to track tightly alongside the torso for maximum lat engagement. The neutral wrist position is comfortable for most trainees and reduces forearm fatigue, allowing greater lat-focused loading than pronated or supinated alternatives.

execution.starting_position: Straddle the T-bar machine. Grip the V-handle or close neutral-grip attachment. Hinge to 45-60 degrees, arms extended.
execution.setup_instructions: Set chest pad to allow full arm extension at the bottom. Keep feet straddling the bar, slightly wider than hip width.
steps: Step 1: Begin hinged with arms fully extended holding the V-handle.
Step 2: Drive elbows back alongside the torso.
Step 3: Row until elbows are past the torso level.
Step 4: Hold 1 second at the top.
Step 5: Lower under control to full extension.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the row. Inhale descending.
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring wide — keep them tucked for lat emphasis
Excessive torso bounce — control the torso angle throughout
safety_considerations: Maintain neutral lumbar spine — do not hyperextend at the top
Use straps if grip limits lat training volume
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension to elbows past torso level.
coaching_cues: Elbows hugging the ribs on the way up
Lead with the elbows, not the hands
Feel the lats at the bottom stretch
